# Finding ∫ x³sin(x) dx

I'll use **integration by parts** repeatedly (tabular method).

## Setup

Let me repeatedly differentiate x³ and integrate sin(x):

| Sign | Differentiate (u) | Integrate (dv) |
|------|-------------------|----------------|
| +    | x³               | -cos(x)        |
| −    | 3x²              | -sin(x)        |
| +    | 6x               | cos(x)         |
| −    | 6                | sin(x)         |
| +    | 0                | -cos(x)        |

## Multiply diagonals (sign × left × right):

$$+1 \cdot x^3 \cdot (-\cos x) = -x^3\cos(x)$$
$$-1 \cdot 3x^2 \cdot (-\sin x) = +3x^2\sin(x)$$
$$+1 \cdot 6x \cdot \cos x = +6x\cos(x)$$
$$-1 \cdot 6 \cdot \sin x = -6\sin(x)$$

## Result

$$\int x^3 \sin(x)\, dx = -x^3\cos(x) + 3x^2\sin(x) + 6x\cos(x) - 6\sin(x) + C$$

## Verification (differentiate):

- d/dx[-x³cos(x)] = -3x²cos(x) + x³sin(x)
- d/dx[3x²sin(x)] = 6xsin(x) + 3x²cos(x)
- d/dx[6xcos(x)] = 6cos(x) - 6xsin(x)
- d/dx[-6sin(x)] = -6cos(x)

All terms cancel except **x³sin(x)** ✓

<answer>-x**3*cos(x) + 3*x**2*sin(x) + 6*x*cos(x) - 6*sin(x) + C</answer>
